head: e54f0974
rerun_rationale: The prior audit assessed gates that were correct but UNREACHABLE: MCP_INLINE_AUTH_ENABLED was wired into zero compose services and could never be turned on, so the 'default-safe posture' was unconditional rather than opt-in. That blocker is fixed on this branch (4 wirings, verified via compose config resolution), making the audited surface genuinely reachable on an opt-in deploy. This pass re-verifies the now-live controls against code.

attack_surface.unauthenticated_reachable: the MCP port's keyless session tier, ONLY when MCP_INLINE_AUTH_ENABLED=true

informational.title: INTERNAL_API_SECRET can act as any verified email
informational.detail: The mechanism the session-not-a-minted-key design requires. Grants nothing beyond internal-secret compromise, which is already backend god-mode over /api/internal/*. Now that the surface is reachable, the operational recommendation was carried into .env.example and requirements mcp.md 7.6: set INTERNAL_API_SECRET explicitly in production rather than relying on the -> SECRET_KEY fallback, so it gets its own rotation lifecycle.

informational.title: Stale docstring recommended the approach that caused a silent total outage
informational.severity: informational (not security — invited failure is availability, not bypass)
informational.detail: Claimed the branch-dependent work on the enumeration-safe /request path runs 'in a worker thread'. It does not and must not: an earlier asyncio.to_thread revision silently stopped every code send (SQLite connections are thread-affine, so _email_is_known raised in the worker and its own fail-closed handler swallowed it into 'unknown address') while still answering 202. The router is the entry-point file, so the natural consistency edit was to reintroduce the outage. Corrected to name BackgroundTasks explicitly and state why a thread is wrong.

informational.title: Transitive npm vulnerabilities in src/mcp-server
informational.detail: npm audit reports 4 vulns (1 high fast-uri, 2 moderate, 1 low), all isDirect:false. This PR changes no dependency file, so they belong to the repo-wide dependabot backlog (12 open alerts). Noted because package.json already carries overrides pinning fast-uri and @hono/node-server, so the override is evidently not fully resolving the advisory — worth a look outside this PR.

controls_verified: flag gates all 4 backend routes via router-level dependencies (404 not 403; no per-route override)
assert_email_may_reach_agent runs first, and on /chat before the idempotency claim
per-call re-gate on email_has_agent_access + connector-enabled; fail-closed on DB error
uniform 403 for both denial reasons (no exists-vs-forbidden oracle, Invariant #8)
account-only login/OTP limiters never touch _ip_key (the #591 fleet-wide lockout class)
/request: constant 202, no audit row, all branch-dependent work in BackgroundTasks, global cap checked before the branch
_email_is_known fails closed; code sent only to a known address (account or agent_sharing entry)
role from whitelist default_role, never forced (#314 silent promotion stays closed)
no credential returned by /verify (session binding is MCP-server memory only)
make_inline_auth_scope folds the verified email in (cross-user replay closed)
build_tool_description is name-only (#846 metadata-leak precedent respected)
OPERATOR_SCOPES allow-list excludes anonymous and connector; scope stays anonymous after login
compose defaults are ${VAR:-false} so an unset .env byte-reproduces pre-#848 behaviour

library_assumption.prior_citation: 4.4.0 (wrong: stale local node_modules; lock resolved 4.8.0 at review, 4.12.1 now)
library_assumption.prior_mechanism_claim: canAccess enforced at tools/call (wrong: canAccess is never re-invoked per call)
library_assumption.actual_mechanism: setupToolHandlers closes over a toolsMap built from the FILTERED list; CallToolRequestSchema handler throws MethodNotFound on a miss — enforcement is by absence from the call map
library_assumption.now_pinned_by: src/mcp-server/src/tool-visibility.test.ts — boots a real FastMCP server + real MCP client, asserts a filtered-out tool is rejected on call AND its body never executes (mutation-checked against the pre-#848 deny-check)

hard_exclusions_applied: transitive dependency CVEs with no change in this diff (N3)

resolved: the un-switchable flag (not a security finding but the reason the prior posture assessment was unconditional)
N2 stale worker-thread docstring (found and fixed this pass)
new: N3 transitive npm vulns, pre-existing on dev, out of diff scope
trend.direction: stable — no new attack surface introduced by the post-review changes; the surface became reachable, and its gates re-verified clean

limitations: AI-assisted scan authored by the change's own author, on a keyless auth surface. Same authorship caveat as the prior audit. Independent assurance requires a fresh-context /cso --diff by someone who did not write the code; the reviewer identified this gap and it remains outstanding. --diff scope means the unchanged codebase was not re-audited.
